title: cewf-1994-world
label: Lightcrest

won.source: Billed the reigning CEWF World Champion in the fed's own October 1994 retrospective column; no title-change document survives.

note: Roger DeCarnac had put his own US Title up against Lightcrest for a World Title shot and was, per the same column, working to regain his belt — the outcome of that World Title challenge is not stated.

title: cewf-1994-television
label: "Flashy" Freddy Massey

won.source: Per the fed's own October 1994 retrospective: won the fed's first Battle Royal to become champion despite a poor record, aided by tag partner Dirk Venom, and held the record for longest TV Title reign.

how: Outlasted the field in CEWF's first Battle Royal.
note: Lost the title to Al Andrewson after a month-long pursuit.

title: cewf-1994-television
label: Al Andrewson

won.source: Per the fed's own October 1994 retrospective: beat Freddy Massey for the Television Championship after chasing it for a month.

how: Beat Freddy Massey after a month-long pursuit, with Massey's own partner Dirk Venom having interfered in earlier bouts between them.
note: Still champion as of the fed's own October 1994 retrospective.

title: cewf-1994-united-states
label: Roger DeCarnac

won.source: Per the fed's own October 1994 retrospective: won the US Title from original holder The Gravedigger.

how: Beat original champion The Gravedigger for the US Title.
note: Put the title up against Lightcrest for a World Title shot and, per the same column, was 'in the process of regaining his belt' as of October 1994 — the current holder at that moment is not stated.

title: cewf-1994-battle-royal
label: "Deadly" Dirk Venom

won.source: Per the fed's own October 1994 retrospective: won the Battle Royal Championship during the fed's European Tour angle, one of at least two Battle Royals he won outright.

how: Won a Battle Royal during the fed's own European Tour angle.
note: Still champion as of the fed's own October 1994 retrospective.
